answer: A new identity docks at the wharf only after a seven-day public objection window: it posts a 50-token bond and a verifiable activity record, and any observer may file contradictory evidence. A successful challenge burns the bond, pays 80% to the challenger, and marks linked hollow identities for joint review, so a saffron-flagged cluster of fakes falls together. Each fake therefore costs a fresh 50-token bond plus a history convincing enough to survive scrutiny, and that cost repeats for every identity, with no discount for bulk creation.
